rationale: C15 is a direct drafting precedent for the child letter. Both letters use the same four-part sequence: identify the prior section 206 order creating a Board of Inquiry; acknowledge receipt and attachment of the Board's report; restate the presidential finding that the dispute affects a substantial industry and imperils national health and safety; and direct the Attorney General under section 208 to petition a federal district court for an injunction and other appropriate relief. The child adapts this concrete language and machinery from an ongoing coal strike to threatened maritime strikes or lockouts. C18 and C14 share the child's maritime-dispute predicate and Board-of-Inquiry terminology, but neither supplies the distinctive Attorney-General injunction-letter structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: On August 17, 1948, by virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947, I issued [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], creating a Board of Inquiry to inquire into the issues involved in certain labor disputes
shared_material.parent_excerpt: On March 23, 1948, by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947, I issued [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], creating a Board of Inquiry to inquire into the issues involved in a labor dispute
shared_material.explanation: Nearly identical opening language establishes the prior section 206 order and Board of Inquiry, with only the dispute-specific details changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: On August 19, 1948, I received the Board's written report in the matter, in accordance with the provisions of Section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947, and the Executive Order. A copy of that report is attached hereto.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: On March 31, 1948, I received the Board's written report in the matter, including a statement of the facts with respect to the dispute and each party's statement of its position. A copy of that report is attached here to.
shared_material.explanation: Both next record receipt of the Board's written report and attach a copy.

shared_material.child_excerpt: As I stated in my Executive Order of August 17, 1948, in my opinion these disputes threaten to result in strikes or lockouts affecting a substantial part of the Maritime industry ... which strikes or lockouts, if permitted to occur, will imperil the national health and safety.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: As I stated in my Executive Order of March 23, 1948, in my opinion this unresolved labor dispute has resulted in a strike affecting a substantial part of an industry ... which strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national health and safety.
shared_material.explanation: The same statutory finding is inserted at the same point, adapted from an existing coal strike to threatened maritime strikes or lockouts.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I therefore direct you, pursuant to the provisions of Section 208 ... to petition in the name of the United States any district courts of the United States having jurisdiction of the parties, to enjoin such threatened strikes or lockouts, and for such other relief as may in your judgment be necessary or appropriate.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I therefore direct you, pursuant to the provisions of section 208 ... to petition in the name of the United States any district court of the United States having jurisdiction of the parties to enjoin the continuance of such strike, and for such other relief as may in your judgment be necessary or appropriate.
shared_material.explanation: This is the distinctive operative instruction, reproduced almost verbatim while changing the injunction target to fit the later dispute.
